title: Allow users to run the painless execute API on a remote cluster shard

timeline.body:
We added a clusterAlias to the Painless execute Request object, so that index
expressions in the request of the form "myremote:myindex" will be parsed to
set clusterAlias to "myremote" and the index to "myindex".

If clusterAlias is null, then it is executed against a shard on the local cluster, as before.
If clusterAlias is non-null, then the SingleShardTransportAction is sent to the remote
cluster, where it will run the full request (doing remote coordination). 

The clusterAlias field is not part a Writeable field - it not included when serializing
to another node. So when the Action is forwarded to a remote cluster coordinator,
it will just get the index name, and no clusterAlias, indicating that it should run the 
Action locally.

A multi-cluster IT test was added for testing these scenarios.

Closes #92126 and Kibana issue [#145861](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/145861)

timeline.message:
Allow uses to run the painless execute API on a remote cluster shard.

We added a clusterAlias to the Painless execute Request object, so that index
expressions in the request of the form "myremote:myindex" will be parsed to
set clusterAlias to myremote and the index to "myindex".

If clusterAlias is null, then it is executed against a shard on the local cluster, as before.
If clusterAlias is non-null, then the SingleShardTransportAction is sent to the remote cluster,
where it will run the full request (doing remote coordination). Note that before forwarding
the request to the remote cluster, we nullify the clusterAlias in the request, so that the
remote coordinator will interpret the request to run it locally, rather than try to lookup
a remote cluster.

Closes #92126 and kibana issue #145861

timeline.body: We have marked this with `>bug` since it is a regression - runtime fields validation against remote indices used to work in a previous version when Kibana used the search Api to perform it. Painless execute should have supported executing against remote indices when Kibana moved to using it. That's why we are backporting this to 8.9.1.
